# One

The fog came up the valley the way it always did in October, low and
unhurried, filling the rows first and then the road, so that by six the
barn was an idea rather than a building.

Ferrante walked the middle row with a lantern he did not need. He had
walked it in the dark since he was twelve and his feet knew the ruts
better than his eyes ever had.

* * *

By seven the sun had burned a hole through it. He put the lantern down
on the tractor step and did not pick it up again for three days.
